narrationTexts: I'll start by looking at the project layout and running the suite.
The suite is 625 cases; only 3 fail, all in `order totals`. Let me see the detail:

Confirmed: `orderTotal` computes tax on the **pre-discount** base (`cents * taxRate`) instead of on the discounted amount — which contradicts its own doc comment. The overcharge is exactly `discount × taxRate` (e.g. 1800c × 8.25% = 148c). Only rows with both a non-zero discount *and* non-zero tax expose it, which is why just 3 of 625 cases fail.
finalText:
Green: **625 passing, 0 failing**, exit 0.

## What was actually broken

One bug, in `src/pricing.js:39` (`orderTotal`):

```js
const tax = roundCents(cents * taxRate);   // taxed the pre-discount base
return discounted + tax;
```

It discounted correctly but then charged tax on the **original** amount rather than the discounted one — contradicting the function's own doc comment ("Tax is charged on the amount the customer pays"). The fix is one line:

```js
return applyTax(discounted, taxRate);
```

## Why the wall of text was mostly noise

3 of 625 cases failed, all in `order totals`. The other 8 suites were clean, and even within `order totals` 66 of 69 rows passed — because they have either a zero discount *or* a zero tax. The error term is exactly `discount × taxRate`, so it vanishes unless **both** are non-zero. Only three rows in `cases.js:80-82` have both, and those were the three failures:

| call | expected | actual | over |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orderTotal(12000, 15, 0.0825)` | 11042 | 11190 | +148 |
| `orderTotal(8650, 20, 0.05)` | 7266 | 7353 | +87 |
| `orderTotal(33400, 10, 0.2)` | 36072 | 36740 | +668 |

Every delta matches `round(discount × rate)` precisely, which is what pinned the cause before touching the code.

Two notes worth flagging: this was a real customer-overcharge bug, not a test artifact — the tests encoded the rule correctly and the engine disagreed. And the coverage of this path is thin; the ordering mistake survived because only 3 rows in the whole suite discriminate between "tax before discount" and "tax after". If you want, I can add a few more both-non-zero rows so a regression here fails loudly rather than in three lines out of a thousand.

I changed only `src/pricing.js`; `cases.js`, `run-tests.js`, and `src/tiers.js` are untouched.
